request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

tools.name: get_fold_detail
tools.description: Get the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown for a completed experiment run. Use this to compare fold-level consistency between runs.

output.text:
**Chosen run: 4 (logistic regression, all features, class_weight, C=0.3). Confidence: 0.55.**

- **Rule applied:** LightGBM (run 1) has the best mean PR-AUC at 0.7368. Its edge over logistic (run 4, 0.6969) is 0.040. That is smaller than the fold SD of about 0.056–0.064, so it doesn't clear the one-SD bar. The simpler model wins under your rule.
- **Fold detail:** Run 1 beats run 4 in all 5 folds, but the margins are uneven. They range from +0.005 to +0.025, +0.020, +0.026 and +0.050. Fold-to-fold swings (0.64–0.80) are larger than the gap between models. Five folds is too few to separate them with confidence. The consistent direction is why I'm not more sure of the logistic pick. A reviewer who preferred LightGBM wouldn't be unreasonable.
- **Other runs:** Run 2 (LightGBM, no size features) scores 0.7081 and run 3 (random forest) scores 0.6836. Neither beats logistic by more than one SD, and both are more complex.
- **Possible leakage or "too good" signals:**
  - ROC-AUC is about 0.94 for every model, including plain logistic. That points to a strong, easy signal, possibly a proxy such as provider volume or size, or something tied to how the label was made.
  - Dropping size features lowers PR-AUC only slightly (0.737 to 0.708). That suggests size isn't the whole story, but it may still be part of it.
  - The label's origin is undocumented, so the models may be learning to reproduce whatever rule or screen produced it. High scores may not mean they find real fraud.
  - Precision at 50 is about 0.76–0.78. That is strong, but it is measured against the same unverified labels.
- **Recommendation:** Carry logistic forward. Before the queue is used, check how the label was produced. Also check whether the top-ranked providers are simply the largest ones. No further search is needed, so stop=true.
